learningObjective: State the role of an operator dispatcher in an ML runtime (selecting an implementation based on device, dtype, layout) versus the role of an executor (issuing work on the device).
stem: In a modern ML runtime such as PyTorch's ATen or an equivalent stack, what is the primary role of an operator dispatcher?

options.text: To synchronize CPU and GPU streams before every kernel launch so that the executor can guarantee sequential consistency across otherwise-asynchronous device queues.
To decide, based on the (op, device, dtype, layout, autograd key) tuple of a call, which concrete kernel implementation to invoke — i.e., to route from a logical op to a registered backend function.
To allocate output buffers on the target device and free intermediate tensors after each op returns, replacing the caching allocator with a per-op allocator.
To perform compile-time fusion of ops that share tensor shapes so that the executor only sees fused kernels instead of individual operator calls.

explanation: A dispatcher is a routing layer: given an operator call at run time, it looks up the concrete implementation registered for the current (device, dtype, layout, autograd state, functorch transform, ...) — i.e., the 'dispatch key set'. The executor then issues that concrete kernel on the device. Allocation, synchronization and fusion are separate concerns (allocator, stream, compiler).

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: cross-stream synchronization is not the dispatcher's job; it belongs to the runtime's stream/event API.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: this is the operator-dispatch pattern found in PyTorch ATen, TensorFlow, and most runtime kernel registries.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: the dispatcher does not manage the allocator; allocation is done by the runtime allocator (e.g., caching allocator).
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: fusion is a compile-time optimization; the dispatcher operates one op at a time in eager mode.

assumptions: A typical eager-mode ML framework with a dispatcher-driven op registry.
nonImplications: Does not imply that the dispatcher is cheap; PyTorch's dispatcher has measurable per-op overhead that motivates tracing/compilation.
Does not imply every framework has an explicit dispatcher; some fully-compiled runtimes have inlined direct calls.
